rulings.challenge_claim: The front-seam warrant and the stated ground for refusing a cut at verse 10 are both contested by the bytes: the onset formula stands behind a subordinating particle inside a chain of it, and verse 10 does carry an explicit vocative addressee after two verses of divine first-person speech; two paired renderings also run short of their whole-verse splices.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Front seam: the opening verse reads כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte) - the messenger formula stands second, behind the particle כִּי (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), and the same particle opens the verse immediately before the seam, כִּ֣י יֶשׁ י֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte), and the ground-clause inside the span, כִּֽי פָדָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.31.11, byte). The particle-prefixed formula shape is unremarkable in itself (sweep: 29 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys), so the defect is not the shape: it is that a particle binding the span's own opening verse back to what precedes goes unnamed at the seam, while the same particle one verse later is the load-bearing ground for refusing the internal cut. A byte-true device straddling a span's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Rejected-alternative ground, refuted: the declined verse opens שִׁמְע֤וּ דְבַר יְהוָה֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.10, byte) - second-person-plural imperatives with an explicit vocative - after two verses of divine first-person report about a third-person group, הִנְנִי֩ מֵבִ֨יא אוֹתָ֜ם (oshb:Jer.31.8, byte) and וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte). At the span's own opening the same noun stands inside a prepositional phrase, בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), as setting rather than as addressee. The declared heuristic entry carrying that sentence does not survive re-derivation. Second ground, under-reaching: a forward bind to the ground-clause attaches the declined verse to the verse after it, both inside the span, so it bears on nothing at the seam between oshb:Jer.31.9 and oshb:Jer.31.10. Tier-3: a setumah is recorded at oshb:Jer.31.9 (single-witness, weak corroboration in the Prophets, never a driver, absence never counterevidence) - it falls at exactly the declined seam, is disclosed as a mark, and is never connected to the seam it weakly corroborates. Quote-gloss parity: both cited pairs are byte-verbatim against the staged folded text, but the renderings cover 89 and 88 percent of whole-verse splices, dropping precisely the head that renders the particle-plus-formula the onset rests on and the tail that renders the closure formula the signal list claims. Verified in the row's favour: every mark disclosure is exact (petuchah at the front-seam verse, setumah inside the span and at the closing verse, one paseq seg at the opening verse, count-only, single-witness), and the wine-lexeme distinction is byte-true - the attested defective spelling stands in 1 verse book-wide, the plene spelling in 0, against 11 verses for the other wine noun - though the claim ships with neither digit.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground 'carries no koh-amar or addressee change of its own' - it is byte-refuted at oshb:Jer.31.10 - and drop the forward-bind clause as decisive, since it attaches the declined verse to a verse inside the same span. The replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original: read back against oshb:Jer.31.10's own bytes it must not deny a vocative addressee there, and it must state the tier-3 setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.9 as weak single-witness corroboration standing at the declined seam. boundary_rationale: name the subordinating particle standing before the messenger formula at the span's own opening verse and disclose it as continuity across the front seam, the same particle the row treats as load-bearing one verse later. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.7 and web:Jer.31.14 to the extent of their splices, so that the head rendering the particle-plus-formula and the tail rendering the closure formula both appear beside the Hebrew they gloss. device_notes: give the wine-lexeme sentence its digits, naming the swept object and unit (attested spelling, verse counts).

rulings.challenge_claim: Two byte-refuted statements carry this unit: the figure named at verse 18 is not newly introduced, and the ground for holding verse 15 to verses 16-17 denies an addressee shift the unit's own preceding sentence describes; an exclusivity sentence also ships without its digit and three renderings run short.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The back-seam statement is byte-false: the name stands in 7 verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys), two of them earlier in this same chapter - בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte) and וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte) - and the second sits inside the span closing at oshb:Jer.31.14, whose own whole-verse splice carries it and whose own prose names the figure. 'Introduced by name' cannot stand as written. The rejected alternative negates its own premise: it concedes a verse-initial messenger formula in second-person address at oshb:Jer.31.16 against third-person report at oshb:Jer.31.15, then decides on the ground that no addressee or topic shift marks the turn. The bytes carry the shift - כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה stands verse-initially and is followed by מִנְעִ֤י קוֹלֵךְ֙ מִבֶּ֔כִי וְעֵינַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Jer.31.16, byte), second feminine singular, where the preceding verse reports רָחֵ֖ל מְבַכָּ֣ה עַל בָּנֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Jer.31.15, byte) in the third person. A setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.15 falls at that same seam (single-witness, tier-3 weak). The hold itself survives on a ground the row does not state: the frame owner does not change across that seam - the divine mouth carries the formula at both verses, with no quoted-prophet or letter-embedded formula anywhere in reach - so a messenger-formula onset alone is not a licensed internal cut under the ruled seam classes, and the second-person answer answers the complaint just reported. The two refuted statements are the row's stated warrant and stated ground, not the only grounds available; the cure is re-grounding, and any change to the seam itself would be a proposal for owner adoption, never author work. Exclusivity discipline: the single-site claim is true on re-run (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, consonantal tier, MT keys) and the boundary sentence carries its digit, but the disclosure sentence repeats the exclusivity with no digit in that sentence; a scope or tier label never carries an exclusivity claim. Quote-gloss parity: three whole-verse splices paired with renderings at 92, 54 and 33 percent; the two short pairs drop the closure formulas the splices carry and the return-clauses the row's own prose narrates in its own words. Verified in the row's favour: the mark and seg disclosures are exact (setumah at the front-seam verse, at the opening verse and at the closing verse; one paseq seg at each of two verses, count-only, single-witness), and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'A new figure, Ephraim, is introduced by name at verse 18' - the name stands in 7 verses book-wide, two of them earlier in this chapter and one inside the span closing at oshb:Jer.31.14 - and restate the back seam on the byte-true change, the divine promise giving way to the figure's own quoted speech inside a hearing-report. The replacement must pass the test that killed the original: a book-wide sweep of the attested spellings must not contradict the sentence. strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground that no addressee or topic shift marks the turn; it is refuted by the second-feminine-singular address at oshb:Jer.31.16 against third-person report at oshb:Jer.31.15. The replacement must not deny the person switch the bytes carry - ground the hold instead on unchanged frame ownership across the seam and on the answer-to-complaint relation, and disclose the tier-3 setumah standing at that seam. device_notes: put the sweep digit inside the exclusivity sentence itself (verse count, book-wide, named object). boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.15, web:Jer.31.16 and web:Jer.31.17 to the extent of their splices.

rulings.challenge_claim: A pointed catchword straddles this unit's own back seam undisclosed, the opening description misplaces the speaker of the first half-verse, and the verse-final closure formula the unit splices is left unengaged.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Cross-seam cohesion: שׁוּבִי֙ stands inside the span at oshb:Jer.31.19 and שׁ֚וּבִי immediately across the back seam at oshb:Jer.31.21 (byte at each); the two coincide once accents are stripped (sweep: 3 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys - oshb:Jer.31.19, oshb:Jer.31.21, oshb:Jer.31.23; 4 verses at consonantal tier). Function differs across the seam, so this is a catchword hook rather than a formula, but a byte-true recurrence straddling the span's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and nothing in the row discloses it. The root carries no single needle in this book, so only the attested forms are counted here and no root-level digit is asserted. Opening description: the verse opens on the divine first-person hearing-report שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי and names the figure in the third person before any quoted speech (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte); both witnesses frame it so. Correction to the challenge's own digit: the quoted speech begins at the FIFTH word, יִסַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.31.18, byte), not the fourth. The row's next clause supplies the correct frame, so the defect is the ordering of the opening sentence rather than a missing frame. Back edge: the span closes on a verse-final נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.31.20, byte), a formula standing in 162 verses book-wide (sweep: 162 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys). The splice carries it, the paired rendering drops it at 93 percent coverage, and neither the signal list nor the prose records it - the strongest available back-edge corroboration, unengaged, at a seam where a discourse-imperative cluster follows, which is exactly the condition under which such a formula corroborates closure. Verified in the row's favour: the type deviation is disclosed as required; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); the inventory records no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; the declared entry that only the closing verse answers is confirmed on the bytes.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: recast the opening sentence - the unit opens with the divine first-person hearing-report and names the figure in the third person; the quoted speech begins at the fifth word of oshb:Jer.31.18. device_notes: disclose the cross-seam form recurrence (the same consonantal form standing inside the span and immediately across the back seam; accent-stripped tier, 3 verses, forms named), stating that the function differs across the seam. device_notes and observed_substrate_signals: record the verse-final closure formula at oshb:Jer.31.20 and the tier-1 onset that follows it, which is the condition that lets it corroborate closure. boundary_rationale: extend the paired rendering at web:Jer.31.20 to the extent of its splice, so the closure formula appears beside the Hebrew that carries it. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: each opening claim read back against the first words of the verse it describes.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam evidence is under-named - the person and gender switch that actually marks the front seam is not stated as such - and two byte-true recurrences straddle both seams undisclosed, one of them qualifying the back-seam framing.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Front seam: the preceding verse speaks of the figure in the third masculine singular, זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ and רַחֵ֥ם אֲֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ (oshb:Jer.31.20, byte), while the span's opening verse turns to second feminine singular address, הַצִּ֧יבִי לָ֣ךְ צִיֻּנִ֗ים and בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte); both witnesses render the switch. The signal list records only a discourse-imperative cluster. Partial correction to the challenge: the row's prose does name the addressee, so the switch is present in substance and missing from the typed signal record and from the seam argument as such, rather than absent from the row altogether. Cross-seam cohesion, front: the pointed form at oshb:Jer.31.21 continues the form standing at oshb:Jer.31.19 (sweep: 3 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys), undisclosed. Back: the span's closing address ends עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte) and the noun returns at once as וּבְעָרָ֔יו (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) and וְכָל עָרָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.31.24, byte), while בְּשׁוּבִ֖י (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) carries the same verbal root across the same seam. Neither hook is disclosed, and a byte-true device straddling the span's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Noted, not charged: תַּמְרוּרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte) and תַמְרוּרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.31.15, byte) are a same-skeleton pair under different pointing and different sense (sweep: 3 verses, consonantal tier, MT keys). It stands in the neighbourhood, not across this span's own seam, and carries no boundary weight. Calibration: the frontier consideration is recorded as not taken here while it is recorded as taken at the neighbouring spans, at a seam that carries no word-event header of any of the book's three shapes; the honestly held clause at the closing verse is a content question and does not answer that point. Verified in the row's favour: the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.31.21 is real, single, sits mid-verse on the going-verb, and is disclosed rather than resolved (single-witness); the setumah pair is exact; no paseq seg falls in the span; the declared entry about the closing verse is confirmed - the same second-feminine-singular addressee continues under a fresh epithet with no speech formula.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals and boundary_rationale: record the person-and-gender switch at the front seam as the seam's evidence - third masculine singular reference to the figure at oshb:Jer.31.20 giving way to second feminine singular address at oshb:Jer.31.21 - not the imperative cluster alone. device_notes: disclose both cross-seam recurrences with their forms and tiers named: the shared form across the front seam (accent-stripped tier, 3 verses) and the cities noun plus the same verbal root across the back seam. frontier_flag_considered: re-examine the setting, given a seam carrying no word-event header inside the poetry-prose alternation where the neighbouring spans record the consideration as taken. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: every seam-side device that recurs across the span's own edges is either disclosed or shown absent from the bytes.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset warrant is byte-true, but the framing that the material turns away from the preceding address is contradicted by two lexical hooks running across the unit's own front seam, and the English half of the onset quote pair drops the title stack the warrant rests on.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. Upheld: the hooks are byte-true and undisclosed. בְּשׁוּבִ֖י (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) continues the form standing at oshb:Jer.31.19 and oshb:Jer.31.21 (sweep: 3 verses, accent-stripped tier, MT keys), and the cities noun the preceding verse ends on, עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Jer.31.21, byte), returns at once as וּבְעָרָ֔יו (oshb:Jer.31.23, byte) and וְכָל עָרָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.31.24, byte). Upheld also: the onset pair is byte-verbatim but the rendering covers 80 percent of a whole-verse splice and drops exactly the head that renders the full title stack the onset claim is built on. Refined: 'contradicted' overstates what the bytes show. The recurrence carries a possessive switch - second feminine singular 'your cities' before the seam against third masculine singular 'its cities' inside the span - and that switch is itself part of the addressee change the row argues. Disclosed properly, the hook corroborates the seam rather than working against it; the defect is a missing disclosure, not a defeated warrant. Verified: the onset כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.23, and the divine mouth is unchanged, with no quoted-prophet or letter-embedded formula in reach; the mark disclosure is exact, including the honest statement of inventory silence across the interior and closing verses (single-witness, tier-3 weak, absence not treated as counterevidence); the declared entry about the following verse is confirmed on the bytes, its two first-person forms belonging to the human speaker.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose the two hooks running across the front seam - the shared verbal root (accent-stripped tier, 3 verses, forms named) and the cities noun - and state the possessive switch from second feminine singular to third masculine singular, so the disclosure records the hook and the addressee change together. boundary_rationale: extend the paired rendering at web:Jer.31.23 to the extent of its splice so the head rendering the full title stack stands beside the Hebrew it glosses. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: read the turn-of-topic sentence back against the last words of the verse before the seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the back boundary is argued only from a recurring days-are-coming incipit absent from the book's tier-1 seam catalog, and the unit's own test for declining a cut at verse 29 applies just as directly to verse 31 without being engaged. The other item: the stated ground for holding verses 29-30 with verses 27-28 is byte-false because the divine first-person voice does not continue past verse 28, and the front-seam device is a widely recurring shape carried without a digit and with a third chapter-internal site undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The two items are distinct in target - one goes to the back-seam warrant and to consistency with the declined internal cut, the other to the rejected alternative's stated ground and to the front-seam device's digit - but they converge on one underlying defect: the row's description of the voice pattern across oshb:Jer.31.27 to oshb:Jer.31.31. Upheld: the rejected alternative's ground is byte-false. The first two verses of the span carry divine first-person forms - וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte), שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי and אֶשְׁקֹ֧ד (oshb:Jer.31.28, byte) - while the last two carry none: לֹא יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte) and אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת ... תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו (oshb:Jer.31.30, byte) are third-person throughout, and both witnesses render them so. Upheld: the front-seam device is typed a refrain and ships with no digit; the shape stands in 15 verses book-wide at the consonantal tier and 5 at byte tier (MT keys), three of them in this chapter - oshb:Jer.31.27, oshb:Jer.31.31 and oshb:Jer.31.38 - and the third site is undisclosed. Recurrence at that density does not by itself found a unit. Upheld: quote-gloss parity. All four splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, but the renderings cover 15, 93, 67 and 100 percent; the 67 percent pair drops the head that renders בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), the very clause the rejected alternative is about, and the 15 percent pair leaves a sixteen-word splice glossed by four rendered words. Refined: the back-seam framing does not survive re-derivation. The seam is under-STATED, not under-warranted - the third-person proverb material gives way to divine first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte), a person shift absent at the internal seam the row declines. The parity argument asserts that the same first-person divine voice stands on both sides of the back seam; the bytes refute that in exactly the way the row's own sentence is refuted, so that argument reproduces the defect it is charging. Also refined: the incipit's absence from the enumerated internal-cut classes is real, but the back seam does not rest on the incipit alone once the bytes are read, and a byte-true ground for holding the proverb material with what precedes is available and unused - the declined verse opens בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), anaphoric to the days named at the span's own opening verse. Verified in the row's favour: the incipit is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.27; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); the inventory records no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; the proverb material is engaged from the bytes with no cross-tradition appeal.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the ground that the same first-person voice continues, which is byte-false at oshb:Jer.31.29 and oshb:Jer.31.30. The replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original - a first-person form check across all four verses of the span - and the byte-true ground available is the anaphoric days-clause opening the declined verse, which binds it back to the span's own opening. boundary_rationale: state the back seam's actual byte warrant, the third-person proverb material giving way to divine first person at oshb:Jer.31.31, instead of resting the edge on the incipit alone. boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals: give the incipit claim its digit and unit (verse counts, tier named) and disclose the third chapter-internal site at oshb:Jer.31.38. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.27, web:Jer.31.29 and web:Jer.31.31 to the extent of their splices. Whether the seam at oshb:Jer.31.29 should be cut is a boundary proposal for owner adoption, not author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the front boundary is warranted only by the same recurring incipit, yet the disclosure describes both edges as carrying unusually strong tier-1 warrant and the batch's only high confidence rating rests on that asymmetry. The other item: the high rating rests on a positional closure claim the bytes refute - the closure formula at verse 34 stands mid-verse with two clauses after it, stands in every verse of the span, and is separated from the following onset by a verse boundary.
rulings.grounds: The two items are the same defect approached from opposite edges: both target the disclosure sentence claiming unusually strong tier-1 warrant at both edges, and the high rating resting on it. Upheld: the positional closure claim is byte-false. At the span's closing verse the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה stands at words 21-22 of 29 and is followed inside the same verse by כִּ֤י אֶסְלַח֙ לַֽעֲוֺנָ֔ם וּלְחַטָּאתָ֖ם לֹ֥א אֶזְכָּר עֽוֹד (oshb:Jer.31.34, byte); a verse boundary then separates it from כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.31.35, byte, verse-initial). Nothing is immediate about it. Upheld: the formula does not discriminate this edge. It stands in all four verses of the span, and the one verse-final occurrence inside the span sits in the middle of it at oshb:Jer.31.32; it stands in 14 of this chapter's 40 verses and in 162 verses book-wide. Correction to that digit's tier label: 14 is a consonantal-tier verse count aggregating three distinct pointed forms (5, 5 and 4 verses at byte tier), not a byte-tier count. Upheld: the unusually-strong characterisation is unsupported at both edges, and the only high rating in this material rests on it. The front edge's stated driver is the incipit, which stands at 15 verses book-wide at the consonantal tier. Refined: the front edge is not warrantless. The third-person proverb material gives way to divine first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte) - a person shift the row never states because its neighbouring sentence asserts the opposite. Read correctly, both edges carry real byte warrant and the closure corroboration is genuinely available under the ruled reading, since a fresh tier-1 onset does follow at the next verse; what fails is the characterisation and the rating, not the seams. Refuted: the sub-arm that the rejected alternative reverses what its verse does. The span carries לֹ֣א כַבְּרִ֗ית (oshb:Jer.31.32, byte) answered by כִּ֣י זֹ֣את הַבְּרִ֡ית (oshb:Jer.31.33, byte) - a not-this-but-this construction whose second half completes the contrast the first half opens - so describing the later verse as continuing that contrast is byte-supportable, and the declared entry there is otherwise confirmed. Verified in the row's favour: the incipit is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.31; the covenant noun chain holds the four verses together; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls inside the span; all four splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, with renderings at 69, 94, 56 and 29 percent.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the sentence claiming unusually strong tier-1 warrant at both edges. State the back edge as the bytes carry it - the closure formula standing mid-verse in the span's closing verse, with a fresh verse-initial messenger formula at the next verse, and the same formula standing in all four verses of the span, so it corroborates rather than discriminates - and state the front edge's actual warrant, the third-person proverb material giving way to divine first person at oshb:Jer.31.31. confidence: lower from high to the rating the restated warrants support, since the high rating rests on the withdrawn characterisation. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.31, web:Jer.31.33 and web:Jer.31.34 to the extent of their splices - the closing pair currently displays only the material standing after the closure formula. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: any positional claim about a formula read back against the word order of the verse that carries it, with the tier named on every digit.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: this unit's own onset is warranted only by a bare koh-amar recurrence, the same kind of signal its own rejected alternative treats as insufficient to justify a second cut one verse later. The other item: the terminal boundary warrant leans on a verse whose ketiv/qere note the unit nowhere discloses, and two of its three whole-verse splices are paired with renderings covering only part of the spliced run.
rulings.grounds: The two items are distinct: one goes to the onset warrant, the other to mark disclosure and quote-gloss parity. Refuted, with the refuting bytes: the two onsets are not the same signal. At the span's own front seam the messenger formula stands where the preceding unit carries none in any of its four verses, and it introduces a different oracle shape - a participial creation epithet closing on the divine name-signature יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.31.35, byte). At the declined internal seam the formula recurs inside a matched pair: אִם יָמֻ֜שׁוּ ... גַּם֩ זֶ֨רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל (oshb:Jer.31.36, byte) against אִם יִמַּ֤דּוּ ... גַּם אֲנִ֞י אֶמְאַ֨ס בְּכָל זֶ֧רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל (oshb:Jer.31.37, byte) - the same protasis-apodosis shape on the same subject. The row's declared entries for the identical-structure ground are confirmed on the bytes, so a first occurrence after a formula-less unit and a recurrence inside a matched strophic pair are materially different, and the equation between them fails. Refined and upheld in part: the narrower observation stands - the onset sentence never states what distinguishes it from the onset it declines, so the distinguishing evidence is available in the bytes but unstated in the row. Upheld: the row puts oshb:Jer.31.38 into its boundary evidence and the inventory records a ketiv/qere note at that verse (single-witness), disclosed in no field. The note has no separately visible unpointed alternate in the staged bytes, while the two verses after it do carry visible unpointed forms, so a reader cannot check that the quoted opening clause falls clear of it; where a note-bearing verse is put into evidence the note is owed. Upheld: quote-gloss parity. All three splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, but the rendering at oshb:Jer.31.36 covers 29 percent and stops at the protasis, dropping the apodosis on which the oath argument rests, and the rendering at oshb:Jer.31.37 covers 86 percent, dropping both the head messenger formula and the closing formula. New finding: a setumah is recorded at oshb:Jer.31.36 (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver, absence never counterevidence) - it falls at exactly the internal seam the row declines. The row discloses it as a mark and never connects it to the seam it weakly corroborates, the same disclosure-connection gap standing at the declined seam of the span that closes at oshb:Jer.31.14. Verified in the row's favour: both onsets are verse-initial and byte-exact; every parashah and seg disclosure matches the inventory exactly (setumah at the front-seam verse, inside the span and at the closing verse; one paseq seg at each of two verses, count-only).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: state what distinguishes the span's own onset from the onset it declines - a messenger formula standing where the preceding unit carries none, introducing a different oracle shape - instead of leaving the onset asserted. The cure must pass the test that killed the original: the distinguishing sentence read back against the four verses before the seam, showing the absence of the formula there. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere note recorded at oshb:Jer.31.38, which the row carries in boundary_evidence_refs, noting that it has no separately visible unpointed alternate in the staged text (single-witness); and connect the setumah recorded at oshb:Jer.31.36 to the internal seam the row declines, as weak single-witness corroboration for the declined alternative. boundary_rationale: extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.36 and web:Jer.31.37 to the extent of their splices, so the apodosis of the oath and the closing formula stand beside the Hebrew that carries them.

supported_sample.claim_checked: that the one-verse span carries no messenger formula, no closure formula and no addressee of its own, and is therefore bounded on both sides by the surrounding divine speech
supported_sample.notes: Re-derived from bytes, independently of the two reviews. The whole verse is seven words, עַל זֹ֖את הֱקִיצֹ֣תִי וָאֶרְאֶ֑ה וּשְׁנָתִ֖י עָ֥רְבָה לִּֽי (oshb:Jer.31.26, byte): no messenger formula, no closure formula, no vocative and no second-person form stands in it, and its two first-person forms belong to the human speaker; both witnesses render them so. Both seam facts hold - the preceding verse is divine first person, כִּ֥י הִרְוֵ֖יתִי ... מִלֵּֽאתִי (oshb:Jer.31.25, byte), and the following verse opens verse-initially with the incipit (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte). The mark disclosure is exact on both halves: a setumah is recorded at this verse and the inventory is silent at the preceding verse (single-witness, tier-3 weak, absence not used as counterevidence); no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note falls at either verse. The sleep noun וּשְׁנָתִ֖י (oshb:Jer.31.26, byte) in this verse is the homograph that produces false year candidates elsewhere in the book, and the row correctly makes no date claim on it. One reservation, not a defect: the neighbour-seam pair cited for the following verse covers 15 percent of that verse and no pointed form is spliced beside it, so the incipit claim at that edge rests on the rendering alone - it is byte-true at the site, verified above, so the row's decision stands.
